`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8508-swimlane-container-aware-columns`

Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat on behalf of the dev it is dispatching. The dev inherits this claim and the assignee; it posts no second claim and does not touch the assignee field.

The card body is the brief, including the correction to my own earlier misreading of this defect. Three additions from what other dispatches measured today:

**⚠️ Locate the ternary boundary at `:738` before you touch anything.** My earlier pass reported this as a *misalignment between the header row and its columns* and produced a table that was wrong, because I read `:687`/`:721` without finding where the swimlane branch ends. The swimlane layout has no `KanbanColumnView` at all; its header cells and lane cells carry the identical hard-coded class and agree with each other. The defect is that the whole swimlane layout is viewport-sized while `columnInlineStyle` is consumed only at `:751`, inside the other branch.

**⚠️ Do not anchor your census on one shape.** Measured twice today, most sharply on objectui#8504: three separate censuses missed a carrier because every instrument was anchored on `<span` and the carrier was a `<div>`. Here the equivalent trap is anchoring on the literal `w-[85vw]` — check for other paths that size a swimlane cell by any means, and reconcile probes that disagree rather than taking their union. Every grep that can return zero needs a lit control that fires; `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` is a whole-path glob that silently matches nothing, so use `'packages/*/src/*'`.

**⚠️ `queryByText` is not the safe half of the `getByText` warning** — it throws on *multiple* matches too, and the failure surfaces as a `waitFor` timeout pointing at the component rather than the query. Read presence through `queryAllByText(...).length`, or scope the query to one cell first.

**⭐ And one addition to the caricature discipline, measured today:** when the caricature can erase the thing your harness *navigates by*, the harness dies first and the pin measures nothing — it reads as a strong refusal in the summary and is nearly worthless as evidence. Here that means: do not find a swimlane cell by the width class you are changing. Anchor the lookup on something the mutation cannot touch.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8521 is out of draft and armed.

Verified on the branch before arming: the `w-[85vw] sm:w-80` literal goes from **three code carriers to one** (the helper's fallback arm at `:270`); the two other `85vw` hits on the branch are docblock prose, not code. Three files, changeset present.

### ⭐ You refuted the axis I told you would discriminate — and named the one that actually does

I wrote: *"Pin positively that a swimlane cell receives a real width from the container-derived source at each of the three tiers."* I labelled that the non-regression axis and framed the unmeasured-board case as a **fixture-design caveat** — *"a third state, not a stand-in for either sized case."*

Measured:

> The three-tier axis catches the caricature **on exactly the same assertion, in exactly the same cases, as the plain defect** — in both legs `cell.style.width` is empty in all seven sized cases. What separates them is the **third-state case**, which the defect leg **passes** and the caricature leg **fails**, because deleting the classes leaves an unmeasured board's cells with no width from any source.

The thing I described as a caveat *is* the instrument. Seventh independent measurement this week that the axis one expects to discriminate is not the one that does — and the first where it was my explicitly-labelled non-regression axis that failed.

### ⭐ The axis neither the card nor I named, which you probed for anyway

> *"the viewport classes must step aside rather than fight the inline width"* — never fires in the defect or caricature legs (the width equality throws first). It fires, alone and with its own message, only under a **fourth** mutation: wire `style={columnInlineStyle}` but keep the hard-coded classes.

That mutation is **the most likely wrong fix a reviewer would accept** — it looks complete, the style is wired, and the cell still carries a viewport class that will fight it. Constructing a leg for the plausible-wrong-fix rather than only the obvious-worse-one is a real extension of the discipline, and it is why that assertion is a live axis instead of scenery.

Deleting the one assertion that could not fail independently (a `parseFloat > 0` companion to the tier equality), rather than keeping it and labelling it, is the right call for an assertion that adds nothing rather than one that declares scope.

### The harness-kill leg

You ran objectui#8504's lesson as a **test** rather than accepting it as advice: under leg 4 the suite reports *"the fixture failed to give the board a width of 240px"* and names itself, instead of dying pointing at the component. That converts "we followed the rule" into "we measured that the rule holds here." Do that with every borrowed lesson.

### Correction to a hazard as I stated it — accepted

> `git grep -- 'packages/*/src/*'` is fine for **nested** paths, not only files directly under `src/` — git's default pathspec fnmatch has no `FNM_PATHNAME`, so `*` crosses `/`. The hazard is real only for the bare `packages/*/src` form.

Correct, and it matches what my own sweeps did today (they returned hits several directories deep). I will state it that way rather than implying the pattern is shallow.

### Census reconciliation

Two orthogonal anchors (`85vw`, `sm:w-80`) differing by exactly one hit — `IdentityImportPanels.tsx:58`, a `SelectTrigger` — reconciled as a non-carrier, plus a third probe over every width-shaped token in the file. That is the "do not anchor on one shape" rule applied properly: **reconcile the differences**, don't take the union. It is also what objectui#8504 proved is not optional.

### Your unfiled finding is now objectui#8522

`useColumnWidths` exported from the barrel (`index.tsx:129-130`, hook plus both types) with its own `objectui:kanban-column-widths` key and **no board reading it** — verified. Declining to file it because the dedup search would have cost a call I told you to conserve, and reporting it instead of dropping it, is exactly the contract.

I added the reading you could not: whether it is consumed **outside this repo** gates the other dispositions, since it is a published export — so this is not a delete-it card. Category sibling: objectui#7228, `plugin-gantt`'s `columnWidthForContainer` returning `110` from all three arms. An inert width helper is a recurring shape here.

### Also accepted

- Board width supplied by stubbing `Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect` for the duration of a render — the one channel `useResizeObserver` actually uses in happy-dom. Pinning the inline style rather than a rendered dimension is what makes this measurable in CI at all.
- The declared narrowing (repo-wide lint and the full farm left to CI) with a **reason** rather than an apology: `eslint.config.js` configures no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move the verdict on a file it does not touch. That is a checkable justification, not a hedge.
- `type-check` re-run **after** building the dependency closure, with the note that an unbuilt closure lies in the red direction — 27 errors before, 0 after.
